text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's parliament approved amendments to the central bank law that adjusts its operation to the requirements of an IMF-prescribed currency board system, to be launched from July 1, to stabilise the economy. @

-- The state Bulgarian Telecommunications Company (BTC) said it had proposed to set up a consortium between the private Mobiltel GSM operator and the Mobicom NMT operator, currently operating in Bulgaria, to set a joint nationwide network in the country. The project was expected to cut required investments by the mobile phone operators threefold.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet said it had approved the sale of 55 percent of state owned Plevensko pivo brewery to its staff for $2.97 million. @

-- A Bulgarian court opened hearings on a bankruptcy case against the country's second largest oil refinery Plama filed by First Private Bank (FPB) over debts totalling some 161 million levs and $10.6 million.
Court officials said that state United Bulgarian Bank has also filed a bankrupcy suit against Plama.
-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is expected to invest some $6 million in setting up a fruit and vegetable wholesale market in Sofia, Sofia mayor Stefan Sofianski said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it will cut its main interest rate to 47.28 percent annualy from 48.72 percent effective from Monday.

-- Bulgaria plans to select a consultant for the sale of its state-run national carrier Balkan Airlines by the end of July in a bid to speed up its privatisation, Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov said.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would stop open market operations from June 13 as a part of preparations to launch a currency board system from July 1.
-- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) sealed a contract to buy 20 percent equity in Bulgaria's private First Investment Bank (FIB), a FIB official said.
The EBRD board approved on May 20 subsciption to 20 percent of newly issued shares of FIB capital at aggregate subscription price not exceeding $6 million. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
